title: Impact of School District Boundaries on Urban House Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Rationale  
• Assignment to the “less-desirable” school district changes discretely at the geographic boundary.  
• Houses infinitesimally close to the boundary on either side should be similar on every dimension except school district quality.  
• Therefore, comparing log house prices immediately to the left and right of the cutoff identifies the causal effect of being in the worse district.

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: Expected potential log prices vary smoothly with distance in the absence of the boundary; any jump at 0 is due to district assignment.  
2. No precise sorting / manipulation: Sellers and buyers cannot perfectly locate on a particular side of the boundary with infinitesimal precision.  

Because treatment status is deterministically tied to the running variable at the cutoff, a sharp RDD is appropriate.

---

## 2. R Code
```r
##############################################################################
# Impact of School District Boundary on Urban House Prices – Sharp RDD
# File: experiments/exp_b/data/s94_data.csv
##############################################################################

# 0) Packages -----------------------------------------------------------------
need <- c("rdrobust", "ggplot2", "dplyr")
new  <- need[!(need %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new)) install.packages(new, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(need, library, character.only = TRUE)

# 1) Read data ----------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s94_data.csv")

# 2) Basic summary ------------------------------------------------------------
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Mean log price left of cutoff:", mean(df$y[df$running_var < 0]), "\n")
cat("Mean log price right of cutoff:", mean(df$y[df$running_var >= 0]), "\n\n")

# 3) Sharp RDD using rdrobust -------------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0
rdr <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff)

cat("Main RD estimate (rdrobust, local linear):\n")
print(summary(rdr))

# 4) Simple local‐linear regression within Imbens-Kalyanaraman bandwidth ------
# (adds transparency and an easily interpretable coefficient on 'treated')
ik_bw <- rdr$bws[1]   # IK optimal bandwidth from rdrobust
loc_df <- dplyr::filter(df, abs(running_var - cutoff) <= ik_bw)

lm_loc <- lm(y ~ treated + running_var, data = loc_df)
cat("\nLocal linear within IK bandwidth (|running_var| <=", round(ik_bw,3), "):\n")
print(summary(lm_loc)$coef["treated", ])

# 5) Robustness – different bandwidths and polynomial orders ------------------
for(bw in c(0.2, 0.5, 1.0)){
  loc <- subset(df, abs(running_var - cutoff) <= bw)
  mod <- lm(y ~ treated + running_var, data = loc)
  cat("\nBandwidth", bw, ": Treated coef =", round(coef(mod)["treated"], 4),
      " (SE =", round(summary(mod)$coef["treated","Std. Error"],4), ")")
}

# Higher-order polynomial (quadratic) within IK bandwidth
lm_quad <- lm(y ~ treated + running_var + I(running_var^2), data = loc_df)
cat("\n\nQuadratic control within IK bandwidth: Treated coef =",
    round(coef(lm_quad)["treated"],4),
    "(SE =", round(summary(lm_quad)$coef["treated","Std. Error"],4), ")\n")

##############################################################################
# End of script
##############################################################################
```

The script:  
• Loads the data.  
• Estimates the sharp RDD with rdrobust (data-driven bandwidth, robust bias-corrected standard errors).  
• Reports the treatment effect at the cutoff.  
• Re-estimates a transparent local-linear model on the same bandwidth.  
• Varies bandwidth (0.2, 0.5, 1.0) and uses a quadratic specification as robustness checks.  

All numerical results are printed to the console.

---

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative.  
Magnitude: A 7 – 12 percent reduction in log house prices (−0.07 to −0.12 in logs) for properties on the “worse” school-district side of the boundary.

Reasoning  
School quality is capitalised into housing values; even controlling for proximity and neighbourhood amenities, buyers pay less for houses tied to a less desirable school. The effect is local (within a few hundred metres of the boundary) and typically ranges around one-tenth in log terms in the urban U.S. housing literature, hence the −0.07 – −0.12 expectation.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy leverages the discontinuity at the school district boundary.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Houses in the less desirable school district exhibit lower log prices.
